last_action: RAYEN HAS ITS OWN DOMAIN, AND THE STORAGE KEYS CAME WITH IT. Live at rayen-garden.vercel.app since 2026-11-12. juniper-navy.vercel.app still serves the same deployment: Vercel keeps an attached .vercel.app domain through a project rename rather than releasing it, so this was additive and no garden was ever stranded — which is the opposite of what was predicted going in. Renaming the Vercel project from juniper to rayen only re-derives the account aliases; the short domain had to be added explicitly, and rayen.vercel.app was already taken by another account, hence rayen-garden. THE FOUR STORAGE IDENTIFIERS WERE RENAMED AT THE SAME TIME AND ONLY BECAUSE OF IT: @juniper/store -> @rayen/store, the juniper IndexedDB database -> rayen, juniper.lastBackupISO -> rayen.lastBackupISO, juniper.garden -> rayen.garden. Browser storage is per-origin, so the new origin was empty: there was nothing to migrate, no migration code was written, and the garden crosses over in a backup file. That is also the one thing that can never change again — every backup file in existence says juniper.garden, so readGardenFile accepts both strings forever, LEGACY_FORMAT is the name of that promise, and src/lib/__tests__/backup.test.ts is the test that holds it. Confirmed load-bearing by removing the compatibility and watching that one case fail. backup.ts had no tests at all before this — the file that decides whether a garden survives was the least covered in the app. Two user-visible strays the first rename missed, both found by grepping rather than by reading: the watering notification title still said Juniper, and the component test still seeded @juniper/store. juniper-design/ BECAME rayen-design/, which was the last Juniper name in the repo: 14 files moved with git mv so history follows, and 25 references updated across the status docs, both READMEs and four source comments. Nothing in the build ever named it, so the only risk was dead links. D4 keeps the August names in its context and decision — those are what the three repos were called then — and tracks the renames in its parenthetical instead. THE CI BILLING BLOCKER IS GONE FROM THE RECORD, AGAIN. It had been closed once already with evidence from both directions, then re-listed by mistake when the status files were brought current on 2026-11-12. The workflow that now targets rayen-web has run green on f661f81, f78147c and 95e741c. THE RESTORE WORKED. The user installed rayen-garden.vercel.app and the garden came back out of the backup file under the new keys, which closes the move and is also the first time the backup path has been proven end to end on real hardware: saved from one origin, read at another. The last-backup stamp at the new origin starts empty because it is stored per origin; it corrects itself on the next save.
next_action: (1) LIVE WITH IT. Everything structural is done and the remaining questions are not answerable by building: whether a fanned deck is the right way to meet your plants each morning, whether the dryness ramp reads at a glance, and whether use happens at all without a reminder (the D13 bet). (2) Decide on a service worker — the manifest alone got it on the home screen and earned the WebKit eviction exemption, but the app still needs the network on first paint each session. (3) Writing, not just reading: the per-plant journal renders but cannot be added to.

blockers.description: Rayen is unvalidated by real use. The deck has been exercised hard but against a demo garden over two days. Whether a fanned deck is the right way to meet eight plants every morning, and whether the ramp reads at a glance, are questions only real plants over real weeks answer.
Rayen has no reminders at all. A deliberate bet (D13) that the deck is itself the reminder, and the only thing that settles it is whether use happens anyway.

There is no service worker, so the installed app needs the network on first paint of each session. The manifest alone was enough for the home screen and the eviction exemption; offline is a separate, unmade decision.
